title: Hi-Res Garment
content: **List of Contents** Hi-Res Garment Hi-Res Garment Settings **Hi-Res Garment ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jO8Y_Ql30So \- Improve general quality of the 3D Garment after completion. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022465108/mceclip0.png) **Hi-Res Garment** tool from the 3D toolbar or navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Hi-Res Garment.** ** Hi-Res Garment Settings ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fdg5gtx0TtM \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022465108/mceclip0.png) Hi-Res Garment tool from the 3D Toolbar and the Hi-Res Properties window will appear. * **Garment YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5ckmMn4XFx4 ** * **Particle Distance** \- Change all Patterns’ **Particle Distance** to 5mm. \- Modify **Tolerance** to decide the range of Particle Distance so that only Patterns with corresponding Particle Distance value will be affected. Patterns with Particle Distance value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected. * **Add’l Thickness - Collision** \- Change all Patterns’ Add’l Thickness – Collision to the default value, 1mm. \- Modify Tollerance to decide the range of Add’l Thickness - Collision so that only Patterns with corresponding Add’l Thickness - Collision value will be affected. Patterns with Add’l Thickness - Collision value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected. * **Avatar YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9LpHc6GMo2Q ** * **Skin Offset ** \- Change all Avatar’s Skin Offset to the default value, 0mm. \- Modify Tolerance to decide the range of Skin Offset so that only Patterns with corresponding Skin Offset value will be affected. Patterns with Skin Offset value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected. * **Simulation YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P1X3T7rNWPQ ** * **Simulation Quality** \- Change the Simulation preset to the default setting, **Complete (Nonlinear).** \- When fabric items other than the Default Fabric is used to the Patterns, the **Complete (Nonlinear)** Simulation preset shows more realistically accurate length and wrinkles of the 3D Garment. Since the Simulation speed decreases when the Simulation preset is changed to **Complete (Nonlinear)** , it is advised to change to the respective preset only when improving the 3D Garment quality. Go back to the List of Contents

title: Render Output Improvement (Graininess, Noise)
content: **Where to Start** Once your garment or look is finished, make sure you use the [Hi-Res Garment tool](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012380608-Hi-Res-Garment) and simulate to see the realistic drape. Next, go to the **Render Menu ▶ Render** to enter the [Render Mode](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014784747-Run-V-Ray-Render). Click to start an Interactive Render. As you view the preview, a good place to start is to use the default settings; ● set up the image size as desired ● use a **plain background** (with an image vignette if desired) ● **PNG file format** is lossless and will therefore give you better quality than the JPEG ● reset the lighting to Default (**Studio Low Contrast**) & activate **ground shadow** (this effect is a must when rendering a full avatar) ● **Windows** users: use the **GPU Engine** ● Noise Threshold set at **0.05** ● Max Render Time = **20 min** ● Light & Material Quality at **Medium** If you start here and create a final render, stop Interactive Render and click Final Render. Watch this complete and take note how long it takes. From here, you can make adjustments to the lighting and render properties to improve the image quality. **Further Considerations** Creating a beautiful image in CLO can be tricky at times. You need to balance the complexity of your project with the limitations of your hardware and the amount of time your computer will take to give you the final result. Here are a few things to consider; ● **How does your hardware match up to our[system requirements](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307168-CLO-system-requirements-March-2024)?** It is better to go towards the _Recommended_ rather than _Minimum_. If your computer matches the minimum requirements, yes, it may work, but it will not be a good experience. You will quickly run into speed limitations not only while rendering, but with simulating as your garments get more complex. The amount of RAM in your computer will make the biggest difference with speed. ● **What materials did you use?** Are there any metals, sparkles, shiny areas on the fabrics, buttons, zippers, snaps, etc.? Anything that will reflect light while rendering can add more time to the rendering process. ● **Have you added accessories or objects in the scene that have glass or metal?** Did you create a “mirror” or place a ground plane that is very shiny? Think about your environment. It may be awesome to have a detailed room around your avatar and garment, but opting for a simple, plain background will not only reduce rendering time, but also focus the viewer’s attention on the garment. ● **How complex is the garment or garments making up the looks?** Is there visible internal layers or multiple layered garments? Are you using lots of buttons, zippers, graphics, prints, etc.? Is there puckering or have you activated Realistic Seamline while using the Fill tool? ● **What image size are you using?** It is recommended you pick from the pixel size options (640 x 480, etc.) as this will reduce the rendering time. The paper size layouts may seem attractive but the document/pixel ratios can cause a slowing of the rendering process. If needed, changing the resolution (ppi) will slow down the rendering process. ● **Check your[Render Properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014899148-Edit-V-Ray-Render-Properties):** ○ Are you rendering **fur**? It is recommended to switch to CPU Engine to get better results, **but** it will take longer. So you need to decide whether the slower rendering is beneficial. ○ What is your **Noise Threshold**? Default 0.05, the lower you go, the better the details **but** it will take longer. ○ **Max Render Time** ; Based on all the variables, CLO will do the best it can with the time you have allotted. ○ **Light** and **Material Quality** will also affect the length of your render. **※****Note: **If you want to render an animation (rather than capturing the 3D window), always do a single render to start. The time it took to render that one image should be multiplied by the number of frames in the animation. ● Example: ○ image rendering time = 5 minutes ○ frames in animation = 450 ○ how long the render animation will take: 2250 minutes or 37.5 hours (a day and a half)
content_description: This page provides essential guidelines and best practices for optimizing your garment rendering process in CLO, ensuring high-quality results while effectively managing rendering time and hardware limitations.

title: Troubleshooting: Vray Render Problems
content: This article describes the causes and solutions to various problems that may occur during V-ray rendering in CLO software. If your CLO rendering is not working, freezing or extremely slow, please take a closer look at this article. And please note that this article does not describe everything related to rendering, but rather describes the main causes of problems and how to mitigate them. ![Lady_in_Hanbok_png.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44490647923481) <The image above is an example of a traditional woman dress rendered using V-ray in CLO software.> ## **Technical background** CLO software includes the [V-Ray Render SDK from Chaos](https://www.chaos.com/vray), allowing users to create photorealistic renders of their projects, including clothing and avatars. CLO's V-ray renderer supports both Windows and macOS, and can complete rendering faster via GPU acceleration, especially on Windows PCs equipped with Nvidia graphics cards. On Windows PCs and Macs without an Nvidia graphics card, rendering will be done via the CPU, and the results of CPU-based and GPU-based rendering will be almost identical. And one good news, starting with CLO v2025.0, GPU acceleration is available for V-ray rendering on Apple Silicon Macs. In the Render Engine list, you can choose GPU (Metal) in addition to CPU. Also note that acceleration performance via GPU (Metal) depends on the specifications of the GPU cores built into the Apple Silicon Mac and the CLO garment file and its properties. ## **Render Properties** ![004_render_properties.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44375524368025) ### Render Engine * **CPU** : This is the default render engine for CLO and will be locked to this engine on Windows PCs and Macs without Nvidia graphics cards. * **GPU (CUDA)** : This is an option for Windows PCs with Nvidia graphics cards. If you have a modern, high-performance Nvidia GPU, you can complete rendering about 2 to 6 times faster than CPU-based rendering. When rendering very light clothing, like a basic CLO t-shirt, there isn't much difference between GPU and CPU render times. GPU rendering is an option to choose when you want to process very complex and heavy garments quickly, and to do so, you need the latest high-performance Nvidia GPUs. * **CPU Supporting** : This feature adds idle CPU resources during GPU rendering to help render faster and smoother. We recommend leaving this option turned on. * **Low GPU Priority** : This will lower the GPU resources consumed during GPU rendering. You can turn this option on if you want to do other image/video work while rendering, but for fast and stable rendering, you may want to leave it off. ### Finish Conditions * Finish Conditions are literally options that determine how the render will be finished. * **Noise Threshold** : This determines how much noise will be suppressed in the rendered result image. The lower this value is, the better the rendered image quality is. However, as more calculations are performed, computing resources and rendering time increase dramatically. **Even with the default value of 0.05, sufficient quality rendering results can be obtained.** If you want to obtain better quality rendered images, try rendering while lowering this value step by step, like 0.05 > 0.04 > 0.03, and check the final quality. At the lowest values ​​near 0.001, it will take a long time to complete the render even on a high-performance computer. * **Max Render Time (min)** : This is a kind of timer, and when the time set here is elapsed, the render engine will stop even if the rendering has not completed yet. Lowering this value will not make rendering complete any faster. So if you set this value too low, you may see a rough rendered image result because it will stop in an unfinished rendering state. **It is actually better to set it to the maximum value of 100 minutes.** ## **Image/Video Properties** ![003_render_image_properties.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44374636184729) ### Image Size * As the image size increases, the amount of pixels the renderer has to process (i.e. the amount of computation) increases, which in turn increases the usage of the CPU, GPU, video memory, main memory, and the time to complete. If you want to render very large image sizes, make sure your computer is powerful enough to handle it, especially with plenty of memory. Most rendering scenarios can be handled well on a PC with around 32GB of memory and/or around 16GB of video memory, but scenarios such as super large image sizes or animation rendering may run into memory shortage issues. * If you need to continuously process sequential image scenes, such as turntable rendering, animation rendering, and colorway rendering, the load on your hardware and memory usage can increase significantly. Even in rendering scenarios that process sequential scenes like this, keep a close eye on memory usage. ## **Interactive Render vs. Final Render** * Interactive Render is a function that instantly renders changes to the scene that occur when you rotate or scale a garment in the 3D window, showing them within the Render window. That is, since it is a mode for fast and instantaneous rendering results, the image quality and details are reduced compared to Final Render. * Final Render is a function that renders based on the current garment and given render settings and saves the result as an image file or video. Even after Final Render is completed, you need to check the result saved as a file, not the result shown in the render window, to confirm the exact rendered result. Additionally, slight differences in image quality, color, and color tone may occur depending on the image/video viewer program. ## **Problem situations and how to solve them** * **"My computer has an Nvidia graphics card but GPU rendering is not enabled"** : This is either because the GPU device is disabled in Windows, the graphics card and monitor are not properly connected, or because of a graphics card driver error. Please check [this web post](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000296768-Graphics-Card-Problems-and-Troubleshooting) for solutions. * **"Can't render with Intel Graphics or AMD GPU?"** : CLO software supports both CPU and GPU rendering, with GPU rendering only available on PCs with Nvidia graphics cards and Apple Silicon Macs. Windows PCs with AMD or Intel graphics cards, and older Intel-chip-based Macs, only support CPU rendering. * **"So slow, rendering has been taking hours"** : Depending on how complex and heavy your project is, your computer's specifications, and the Render Finish Conditions described above, the render completion time will vary. Try rendering again after loosening the details and properties of the garment itself, as well as the render properties. * **"Freezing or crash happens while rendering"** : As above, it is a result of the complexity of the project, computer specifications, and rendering properties. Sometimes, crashes or rendering failures may occur due to graphics card driver errors, in which case, try updating to the latest graphics card drivers. * **"It shows out of video memory error"** : This occurs when there is not enough video memory to complete the rendering. Please readjust the render properties and image size, close all other programs using video memory, and then try rendering again. For example, starting Windows and opening just a web browser can take up about 600MB to 1GB of video memory. Under these conditions, if your graphics card has 8GB of video memory, your CLO will only be able to use about 7GB of video memory. So if you are running multiple programs in addition to the CLO software, it is recommended that you close them before rendering, as the CLO renderer may run out of video memory. * **"Rendering stops with an unknown error message"** : This is due to a setting error in Windows itself and/or a graphics card driver error. Update to the latest graphics card driver. * **"Garments containing fur and/or knitwear fabrics cannot be rendered, or it shows unexpected render results"** : Fur and knitwear rendering are among the most hardware-intensive of CLO's features. They require several to tens of times more calculations and use more memory than other clothing renderings. If your computer is struggling to handle this scenario, consider designing approaches that use images or textures to represent fur and knitwear. * **"GPU render results are slightly different from CPU render results"** : This is due to the nature of the V-Ray render SDK and may occur when rendering scenes with a large number of light sources and reflections, and very complex fabrics such as fur. This is a known issue for the CLO team and are continuously working on improving it. * **"V-Ray render cannot run because the required V-Ray library could not be loaded in the current environment"** : The CLO software is designed to load configuration files when starting vray-render. This error indicates that essential files for vray-render could not be loaded due to file permissions. The solution is to install the CLO software with administrator privileges, see [details here](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/17074279996697-Disk-access-rights-required-when-CLO-is-running#:~:text=to%20download%22%20appears.-,Windows,-1%C2%A0%20After%20logging). Security programs, such as antivirus programs, may restrict the execution of the CLO software or various files that comprise CLO. In the detailed settings of the installed or running security program, change both the execution of the CLO software and Internet connection to "Allow." ![008_vray_lib_load_fail.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/54219419608473) ## **How to check GPU and video memory usage** * You can check CPU, Memory, GPU, and GPU memory usage in the Performance tab of Windows Task Manager. Below, running just Windows and a web browser, you can see very low CPU and GPU usage, but you can see that the base memory usage is quite high. * When you run CLO to perform tasks like pattern editing, simulation, rendering, etc., you will see increased CPU, GPU, and memory usage. And it is normal for CPU and GPU usage to be close to 100% during simulation and rendering, and GPU usage will not stay at 100% during GPU-rendering. While GPU rendering, GPU usage continues to fluctuate because it is divided into sections where the GPU works, sections where the CPU works, and sections where they work simultaneously. ![007_GPU_usage.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44417445932569) The image above is what Windows Task Manager looks like during interactive-GPU-rendering. The Windows desktop PC specifications and project file details used for testing are as follows: * AMD Ryzen™ 9 7950X Processor (native 16-core), Nvidia RTX™ A6000 (vram 48GB), 64GB DDR5 memory, NVMe SSD 512GB, 4K resolution monitor, wired internet connection * Windows 11 Pro version 24H2 (OS Build 26100.3476), CLO v2024.2.328 * A traditional dress made of multiple layers, particle distance from 5 to 20, no trim, made with 55 patterns and 1144 sewing lines. Check out the links below for file download and tutorial. * CONNECT store: <https://connect.clo-set.com/portfolio/99263/collection/collections?itemId=5af7734d050c4e31987061fbf697a3a9> * YouTube tutorial: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T_UbvoshTpA> **1) CPU** : shows CPU usage. It doesn't always use 100% during rendering and it fluctuates. **2) Memory** : this is the total amount of memory used by Windows, the web browser, and CLO rendering. Windows itself uses about 4GB of memory, and the web browser uses about the same amount. The CLO software uses about 5 to 6GB of memory to do this level of garment rendering. Memory usage will vary depending on OS, hardware configuration, active programs, CLO garment files, and properties. **3) GPU** : shows GPU name and current usage. If you have a laptop or desktop with both integrated graphics and a discrete graphics card, you will see more than one GPU listed. As with CPU usage, it is not always 100% and fluctuates. **4) Dedicated GPU Memory** : shows the total amount of video memory installed on the graphics card and the currently used amount. Windows itself typically uses about 600MB to 1GB of video memory, and web browsers and other programs with graphical UI use a similar amount of video memory. Rendering in CLO typically starts at around 3GB of video memory, and can even use 20GB or more for very complex, continuous image processing scenarios such as animation rendering. Mac users who want to check hardware resources while running CLO software can use the [Activity Monitor](https://support.apple.com/guide/activity-monitor/welcome/mac) app which built in macOS. ## **See also** * [CLO system requirements](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307168-CLO-system-requirements-March-2025) * [Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000296768-Graphics-Card-Problems-and-Troubleshooting) * [How to workaround errors caused by faulty GPU drivers](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/44142966593177-How-to-workaround-errors-caused-by-faulty-GPU-drivers-Last-modified-Mar-2025) * [How to speed up CLO](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/23390057463577-How-to-Speed-Up-CLO)
content_description: This web page aims to provide CLO software users with a comprehensive guide to diagnosing and resolving common V-ray rendering issues, ensuring smoother and more efficient rendering experiences.

title: Auto Fitting
content: ### **Objective** Automatically fit patterns to an avatar's size. **※ Note:** Auto Fitting is supported with CLO avatars and any custom avatars that have a [Fitting Suit](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/24451580024601-Create-the-Avatar-Fitting-Suit-ver-7-3) applied. **※ Note:** This feature was previously called Auto Grading (v 7.2 and below). **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Auto Fitting** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Auto_Grading.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360043525114) **Auto Fitting** ### **Operation** 1. Adjust the [avatar size](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360013257553-%EC%95%84%EB%B0%94%ED%83%80-%EC%82%AC%EC%9D%B4%EC%A6%88-%EC%A1%B0%EC%A0%88-ver5-0-0-%EC%9D%B4%EC%83%81-) and drape 3D garments on the avatar. **※ Note:** Please set Particle Distance as 20mm for the most optimized result. 2. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Auto Fitting** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Auto_Grading.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360043525114) **Auto Fitting ** → The Auto Fitting window appears. 3. Adjust the below options as needed and click OK. **Maintain Pattern Curvature(%)** | Configure the extent of modification of pattern curvature. Higher the value is, less affected curvature while resizing the patterns. On the other hand, lower the value is, both curvature and size of the patterns are modified. ---|--- **Maintain Graphic Size** | ON | Graphics maintain their size. OFF | The size of graphics are adjusted based on the size changes of the patterns. → The 3D garment is auto-fitted and [draped](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034333873-%EC%9E%90%EB%8F%99-%EB%93%9C%EB%A0%88%EC%9D%B4%ED%95%91) on the avatar.
content_description: The purpose of this webpage is to guide users in automatically fitting patterns to their avatar's size using CLO software, ensuring optimal garment draping and customization options.

title: Tape Measure
content: ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55718294111129) **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55718301943193)** #### ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55718294114457)**Tape Measure (Point-to-Point)** #### **Objective** Measure the precise distance between two points on the fabric layout to verify alignment, pattern matching, or spacing between nested pattern pieces. **Location** Print Layout Editor ▶ Vertical Toolbar ▶ **Tape Measure (Point-to-Point)** * * * ### **Operation** 1. **Select Tool** : Click the **Tape Measure (Point-to-Point)** icon from the vertical toolbar. 2. **Define Start Point** : Click on a point, edge, or specific location on a pattern piece to establish the beginning of the measurement. 3. **Define End Point** : Click on a second point (either on the same pattern piece or a different one) to finish the measurement. * A dashed green line will appear, displaying the distance between the two points in the current unit of measure. 4. **New Measurement** : Click again to start a new measurement. **📝********Note:** Only one active measurement is displayed at a time; creating a new start point will clear the previous measurement.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on using the Tape Measure (Point-to-Point) tool in the Print Layout Editor to accurately measure distances between points on fabric layouts for precise alignment and pattern matching.

title: Is it possible to have an Avatar that has the exact specs as my fit model?
content: **Question** Is it possible to have an Avatar that has the exact specs as my fit model? **Answer** Yes. You may modify and use the default Avatar if the Avatar's size can be approximately the same as your fit model. Also, you may purchase an Avatar similar to your fit model in [CLO-SET CONNECT](https://connect.clo-set.com/). However, you need to customize your Avatar through 3D modeling companies if the Avatar's size needs to be exactly the same as your fit model. If you would like to customize your Avatar, please contact the [CLO Global Support Team](https://www.clo3d.com/contact).
content_description: Explore how to create an Avatar that matches your fit model's specifications, including options for modifications and customizations.

title: 7.3 New Feature List

content: **Objective** Compare the length of two segments of different Patterns in real-time by temporarily aligning each other. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K9VQY4VAi7g ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Walk Pattern**** **2D Toolbar ▶****![pattern_walking.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36790602293657)**Walk Pattern** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Walk Pattern**** **2D Toolbar ▶****![pattern_walking.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36790602293657)**Walk Pattern**** ** 2. Click on a point or a part of a pattern outline. → The point or the part of a pattern outline is selected and an arrow appears in between the selected point and the mouse cursor. 3. title: CLO File Formats
content: **See below a list of CLO-internal file formats.** **Type** | **Format** | **Description** ---|---|--- **Arrangement Points** | *.arr | Arrangement points are the blue points that may be distributed around an avatar and are used to easily arrange patterns around it. They are created on top of bounding volumes (*.pan) covering the surroundings of the avatar. **Alvanon Avatar** | *.avac | Alvanon avatar file format. **Alvanon Avatar Pose** | *.avacp | Pose file for Alvanon avatars. **Avatar Size** | *.avs | Contains avatar size information. A compatible avatar file (*.avt) must be loaded before opening an avatar size file. **Avatar** | *.avt | Contains all information related to avatars (model/mesh, sizing data, pose, motion, shoes, hair, glasses, bounding volumes, arrangement points...) **Avatar (encrypted)** | *.avte | Encrypted CLO avatar file. **Avatar (encryption permission)** | *.avtp | Permission key file to unlock encrypted avatars. **Buttonhole** | *.bth | Contains type, size, color, etc. of buttonholes. **Button** | *.btn | Contains type, size, color, etc. of buttons. **Camera Motion** | *.cak | Contains camera motion animation data. **User Settings Configuration** | *.cfg | Stores user configuration settings. **Camera Projection** | *.cmp | Contains the camera's field of view information (distance, etc.) **Camera Transformation** | *.cmt | Contains camera view information of the 3D garment window. **Camera Properties** | *.cpt | Contains camera properties. **Graphic Properties** | *.grp | Contains the properties of a placed graphic. **Hand Pose** | *.hpos | Save or load only the hand pose instead of the entire pose of an avatar. **Body Measurement** | *.mea | Avatar body measurement file. **Joint Motion** | *.mtn | Contains avatar motion information. As with the pose file, it can only be saved on COLLADA file avatars with joint and animation information. **Pattern** | *.pacx | Contains pattern pieces only without any simulation data. **Bounding Volumes** | *.pan | Bounding volumes are the green cylinders or boxes covering each part of the avatar, and each end of such a shape is connected to an avatar's joint. Therefore, even if a pose is changed, the cylinders/boxes adjust to the changed pose. **Pose** | *.pos | An avatar's pose can easily be changed with this file. Avatar poses from other software can only be saved if the avatar is a COLLADA file with joints. **Print** | *.prt | Contains any property values (configuration, color, maps...) of a print added to a fabric via the print feature in the Object Browser. **Physical Property** | *.psp | Contains detailed values of a fabric's physical properties. **Puckering Style Preset** | *.ptp | Saves puckering style presets used for topstitching or seam visualization. **Render Camera Properties** | *.rcp | Contains camera properties for rendering scenes. **Simulation Property** | *.smp | Contains settings for simulation. **Topstitch** | *.sst | Contains type, number of lines, thread thickness, SPI, length, etc. **Trim** | *.trm | Contains all trim object data. **Light Properties** | *. vlp | Defines light properties for rendering scenes. **Image/Video Properties** | *. vmp | Includes image or video rendering settings. **Render Properties** | *. vrp | General render settings including resolution, quality, and environment. **Avatar Accessories** | *.zacs | Hair, shoes, glasses, jewelry, etc. compatible with an avatar. **Modular Block (OLD)** | *.zblc | Deprecated; modular block format used in earlier versions. **Custom View** | *.zcmr | Custom camera views saved by the user for consistent shot framing. **Fabric** | *.zfab | Contains any property values (maps, color, physical properties...) of a fabric. **Modular Template (OLD)** | *.zmdr | Deprecated; format for modular garment templates used in earlier versions. **Modular Block** | *.zmod | Modular block design file used for creating reusable garment modules. **Garment** | *.zpac | Contains 3D garments in their simulated state, 2D patterns, seamlines, fabrics, other materials, etc. **Zipper Puller (OLD)** | *.zpl | Deprecated; zipper puller model data. **Project** | *.zprj | Compresses the various files used for garment creation into one, containing the AVT file that has avatar-related data, the ZPAC file that contains garment-related data, as well as animation data if applicable. **Zipper Puller** | *.zpu | Zipper puller texture mapping file. **Zipper Slider** | *.zsd | Zipper slider model data. **Scene & Props** | *.zse | For stages and props to add to the 3D scene. **Zipper Slider** | *.zsl | Zipper slider texture mapping file. **Zipper Stopper** | *.zsp | Zipper stopper geometry file. **Zipper Slider & Puller** | *.zss | Combined zipper slider and puller mapping file. **Render Properties (all combined)** | *.zvrp | All-in-one render properties file combining light, camera, image/video, view settings, etc. ****
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive reference for CLO-internal file formats, providing details on each format's type, description, and usage within the CLO environment.

title: Adjust Collision Thickness
content: #### Simulation thickness is invisible set property that represents the collision limit for Garments to result smooth Simulation. **📝********Note:** For the same reason, the default value of Avatar thickness (Skin Offset) is set for 3mm. For form-fitting Garments or accurate fitting measurement, it is recommended that [Skin Offset](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002227387) is adjusted alongside the Simulation thickness. 1. Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Add'l Thickness-Collision** 2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/60054353315481) **Collision Thickness** has been improved so that its thickness direction matches **Rendering Thickness** , ensuring that the visible thickness and simulation collision are applied consistently.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the Simulation Thickness and Skin Offset settings in garment design to ensure smooth simulations and accurate fit.

title: Alvanon Avatar (AVAC) Open
content: ### **Objective** Load purchased certified Alvanon Avatar into CLO. **📝****Note:** To successfully load an Alvanon Avatar, it must go through a certification process. Loading an avatar without certification will restrict simulation and file saving. **Location**** **Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶**Avatar** (Ctrl+Shift+A) **Operation** 1. Click the tool/menu in Location → The Open File window will appear. 2. Select the Alvanon Avatar file to be loaded and select **OK**. → Alvanon authentication window will appear. 3. Complete the certification process by entering of **Alvanon Body platform** ID/FW → If certified successfully, the avatar will be loaded.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for successfully loading a certified Alvanon Avatar into CLO, ensuring compliance with the necessary certification process.

title: Set Color Theme
content: **New in CLO 2024.2. ** Set the theme to Dark or Light based on your preference and environment. **Dark theme** uses a dark background for the user interface, reducing eye strain and glare, especially in low-light environments. It helps to keep the overall brightness of the screen lower, which can be more comfortable during prolonged use. **Light theme** , on the other hand, features a bright background that provides a clean and crisp appearance, improving readability in well-lit environments. **** 1. Click on the **Setting » User Settings** in the menu bar. 2. Set the theme under **User Interface > Appearance**. ** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37041977442841) ****** 3. Restart CLO to apply the theme.
content_description: Discover how to customize your viewing experience in CLO 2024.2 by choosing between the Dark and Light themes to suit your environment and reduce eye strain.

title: Add & Apply Fabric Style
content: **List of Contents** Add a Fabric Apply a Fabric Group Setting (ver 7.1) How to Delete a Fabric **Objective** Add fabric style and apply it to the garment. ![2025-10-13 16_46_49-CLO Network OnlineAuth.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51497099027097) **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab **Operation ** **How to Add a Fabric** Select the Fabric tab in the Object Browser * **The Add Button** * Click **Add** at the top right. * A Default Fabric will be added. * **The Fabric Library** * Open the CLO Fabric Library * Double Click the Fabric (.zfab) or click & drag the fabric and drop into the Fabric Tab. * A Default Fabric will be added. **How to Assign a Fabric** Select the Fabric tab in the Object Browser * **Assign to Selected Patterns Button** * Select a pattern(s) then click the **Assign** button to the right of the Fabric. → The Fabric is applied to the pattern. * **Drag and Drop to Assign** * Drag the fabric directly onto the pattern piece in either the 2D or 3D window to apply it. → The Fabric is applied to the pattern. **Group Setting (ver 7.1)** * To set Fabric Groups, Click the **Create New Folder** button at the top left of the Fabric tab. → A new folder group is created. * Click the **Add Fabric** or **Open Fabric Files** buttons on the right side of the group to load the Fabric file. → A Fabric style is added or opened to the group. * Click the **Edit Folder Name** button on the left of the group to edit the name. Or drag the Fabric style to another group to change the group. **How to Delete a Fabric** A fabric in the Object Browser can only be deleted if not assigned to any pattern pieces in your 2D/3D workspace * **Delete Icon** * Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51497099033497) **Delete** icon next to the Fabric Item. → The Fabric is deleted from the Object Browser * **Delete Option from Right Click Drop Down Menu** * Right Click on the Fabric to be deleted and select Delete from the Drop Down Menu → The Fabric is deleted from the Object Browser * **Delete Key on Keyboard** * Select the fabric to be deleted and press the **Delete** key on the keyboard → The Fabric is deleted from the Object Browser Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to add, assign, group, and delete fabrics in CLO software for garment design.

title: Edit Texture Size (Property Editor)

Find the **Transformation** option which only appears [when a texture is applied to a Pattern.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000471388-%EC%9B%90%EB%8B%A8-%ED%85%8D%EC%8A%A4%EC%B2%98-%EB%84%A3%EA%B8%B0) **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Angle** | Type in the rotating angle. **Width** | Set the texture width. **% (ver5.0.0)** | Configure the texture width with percentage. **Height** | Set the texture height. **% (ver5.0.0)** | Configure the texture height with percentage. **Lock Aspect Ratio** | Lock the width and height ratio.

title: How to successfully make payments: Applicable for the users with Indian Bank accounts & Cards.
content: **Note-**_According to the RBI Guidelines, Debit/Credit Cards issued to customers including new, reissued, renewed or upgraded cards, will be enabled for Domestic ATM and Point of Sale (POS)/physical transactions only. The cards will be disabled for Online, Contactless and International transactions to protect against fraud. In addition, if customers have not used their existing card for online, contactless or international transactions in the last 3 years (including card issues or new accounts opened during this period), usage for these purposes will be mandatorily disabled. However, the limits can be set up & the usage can be enabled for any disabled transaction by simply logging into respective Bank Online or Mobile App._ **Steps for enabling “International transactions” are as follows:** **HDFC Bank** **Mobile App*** Step 1: **Login** to HDFC Mobile Banking App. Step 2: **Select ‘** Pay’ > **Select** ‘Cards‘ from the main menu. Step 3: **Select** 'Debit Card’ > **Select** ‘Customized’. Step 4**:****Scroll & Select** ‘International’ > Enable the ‘Disabled’ option > **Select** ‘Confirm’. Step 5: **Check and Enter** the OTP received on your registered mobile number. **Net Banking*** Step 1: **Sign-in** to HDFC NetBanking. Step 2: From your dashboard, **Select** ‘Cards’. Step 3: **Select** ‘Debit Cards’. Step 4: **Select** ‘Request’. Step 5: **Click** on ‘Set international Usage’. Step 6: **Select** ‘Card to be enabled for International use’. Step 7: **Enter** any additional card details if requested & **select** ‘submit’. **ICICI Bank** **Mobile App*** Step 1: **Login** to the iMobile App. Step 2: **Select** ‘Credit/Debit Card’ > **Select** ‘Manage Card’ from the main menu. Step 3: **Select** ‘Credit/Debit Card’ for which international transactions are desired. Step 4: Under ‘Manage Card’ > **Select** ‘Transaction Settings’. Step 5: **Select** ‘International’ > Click to continue. Step 6: **Select** ‘Confirm’ to allow international credit card transactions. **Net Banking*** Step 1: **Open** https://www.icicibank.com/ > **Select** ‘Personal Banking’ option. Step 2: **Login** by adding your NetBanking ‘User ID and Password’. Step 3: **Select** ‘Cards and Loans’ from the main menu > **select** ‘Credit/Debit Card’ from the sub-menu. Step 4: **Select** ‘Manage Card’ > **Scroll & Select** the ‘International Section’. Step 5: **Tap** to ‘Enable’ and manage limits of the transaction for ATM, Online, Merchant Outlet, etc. Step 6**: Submit** by verifying with OTP to activate international transactions. **KOTAK Mahindra Bank** **Mobile App*** Step 1: **Login** to Kotak Mobile Banking App. Step 2: In ‘Service Request’ **Select** ‘Debit Card’. Step 3: **Select** ‘Card Control’. Step 4: **Scroll & Select** your ‘Debit Card Number’. Step 5: **Select** ‘International/Domestic Controls’. Step 6: **Select** ‘On/Off’ for International Usage. **Net Banking*** Step 1: **Login** to Kotak Net Banking. Step 2: **Select** the “Debit Card section’ Option. Step 3: **Select** ‘Card Control’. Step 4: **Enable** ‘International Usage’ on ATM withdrawal, Transactions at retail outlets/merchant stores and E-Com transactions. _*You can also set your daily International ATM, POS and ECOM transaction limit according to your preference. Simply change your ATM, POS and ECOM limits in ‘Limit Management/Controls’ on Kotak Mobile Banking App or Kotak NetBanking page. *_ **SBI- State Bank of India** **Mobile App* (Yono)** Step 1: **Login** to Yono Mobile App. Step 2: **Select** ‘Services’. Step 3: **Select** ‘Manage Debit Card’. Step 4: **Select** your ‘Account’ from the dropdown Step 5: **Select** your ‘Debit card number’. Step 6: **Scroll & Enable** the ‘International usage’. **Net Banking*** Step 1: **Login** to SBI NetBanking. Step 2: **Select** ‘Services’ from the main menu Step 3: **Select** ‘Manage Card Usage’. Step 4: **Change** the transaction type from ‘Domestic’ to ‘International’ **CITI Bank** **Mobile App*** Steps to Enable your card for international transactions. [Enable your Citi Card for Online, Contactless and International Transactions (citibank.co.in)](https://www.online.citibank.co.in/citihelp/topics/cards/transactions-security-enhancement/index.htm#:~:text=You%20can%20enable%20your%20card%20for%20international%2C%20contactless,International%20usage%20or%20setup%20limit%20for%20Online%20transactions)
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for customers to enable international transactions on their debit and credit cards, in compliance with RBI guidelines, ensuring enhanced security and fraud protection.

title: [Important Notice] Student Account Review
content: As part of our ongoing account review process, student members who have received student discount benefits for a period of four years are required to undergo additional verification to extend their discount benefits. Please review the information below regarding the next steps for your account. **IF YOU HAVE ALREADY GRADUATED:** Cancel your student plan if they are still active (you can use all of the remaining days before the license expires). Before canceling, be sure to save all files to a local drive to prevent data loss. To continue with a CLO subscription: * Sign up to clo3d.com using your personal email, and re-subscribe to a plan of your choice. Or * If your student account is integrated with CLO-SET with NO ACTIVE subscription, you can simply request [Change Email from CLO-SET](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/31866962710169-Change-Email-from-CLO-SET) to a new email address and proceed to subscribe to a plan of your choice. **IF YOU ARE STILL IN SCHOOL:** Please subject the following documents to [Contact Us](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus) for verification: 1\. A copy of your official enrollment letter, including an official academic stamp, or a current class schedule that shows your name. 2\. A copy of your current student ID card. Upon approval, we will extend your student account for an additional 2 years. _Please note that after this period you will no longer be eligible for a student discount, as we have a six-year cap on student accounts._ **DEADLINE:** To avoid interruption of service, please ensure we receive your enrollment documentation before the date that's provided via your email. If we do not receive your submission by that date, your student account will be canceled immediately. If you have any questions or need further assistance, please don't hesitate to reach out via [CONTACT US](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus).
content_description: This webpage provides essential information and next steps for student members to verify their accounts and extend their discount benefits as part of the account review process.

title: Apply Linked Editing – Instance Pattern
content: **List of Contents** Instance Pattern Apply Instance Pattern Remove Instance Pattern **Instance Pattern** \- Edit identical Patterns simultaneously. ** Apply Instance Pattern** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=89gLqS2ZxZM \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. \- Right-click on the Patterns to be linked and select Apply Linked Editing – **Instance Pattern** from the pop-up menu. \- The linked Patterns will be highlighted in yellow-green. \- The linked Patterns can be edited at the same time. **Remove Instance Pattern** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n99HbrpHdhI \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png)**Edit Pattern** tool. \- Right-click on the Patterns to be unlinked and select **Remove Linked Editing** from the pop-up menu. \- The linked Patterns will be separated. \- The Patterns can be edited individually. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides instructions and video tutorials on how to apply and remove the Instance Pattern feature for simultaneous editing of identical patterns in the design software.

title: Custom View
content: Add Open/Save Overwrite/Rename/Delete Load Display State Mode #### Easily open and save a custom view of the 3D window at your convenience. #### **Add** 1. Right-click on the 3D background and click the **Custom View** menu. 2. Click ![camera.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44249824664985) **Add Current Viewpoint** in Custom View window. 3. Click on the added custom view to instantly switch to it. #### #### **Open/Save** 1. Click ![Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44249824666137) **Save** / ![Button-1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44249824667033) **Open** to manage Custom Views as ZCMR file. #### #### **Overwrite/Rename/Delete** 1. Right-click on the added custom view 2. Right-click on the added Custom View to overwrite it with the current view, rename it, or delete it. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59642709689113) #### **Load Display State Mode** 1. Click ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59642726389785) **Load Mode** to select the preferred state option when adding Current Viewpoint. **Load Mode** | **Description** ---|--- **View Only** | The 3D state is not loaded. Custom view only moves the camera, preserving the current window's display states. **View with Display Settings** | The 3D state is loaded. Custom view applies both camera position and saved 3D display states. #### Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on managing custom views in a 3D environment, including adding, saving, overwriting, renaming, deleting, and loading display states for enhanced user experience.
